messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

The owner needs help. Add an `agent` role and let admins invite other admins or agents:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitations

{"invitation":{"email":"sam@example.test","role":"agent"}}
```

Return an `invitation` and email a link to `/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN` on the
frontend. Let admins list and inspect invitations, resend them with `POST /invitations/:id/resend`,
and revoke them with `DELETE /invitations/:id`. Track pending, accepted, revoked, and expired
invitations. Don't create competing invitations or let customer registration take a pending invite's email.
List invitations by ID ascending.

The acceptance screen uses `POST /invitation_previews` with
`{"invitation_preview":{"token":"TOKEN"}}` to show the invited email, role, business name, subdomain,
and expiry inside `invitation_preview`. Then it submits:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances

{"invitation_acceptance":{"token":"TOKEN","name":"Sam","password":"my-team-password"}}
```

Return `user` and `account`; Sam can sign in without another verification email.

Admins also need `GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, and `PATCH /users/:id`. Include `suspended` on users
and support `{"user":{"suspended":true}}`. Suspension revokes sessions and clears assignments.
Don't let admins suspend the last active admin. Filter users by role or suspension, and invitations
by status. `GET /staff` supplies active staff choices for assignment controls.
List users and staff by ID ascending.

Staff can assign tickets with `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":12}}` or clear them with null. Include
`assignee_id` and the assignee's ID/name on tickets. Both admins and agents can work on the business's
tickets, but only admins manage people.

Add private notes through the existing comment input, for example
`{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Checking this with billing.","public":false}}}`.
Internal activity must not change the customer-facing request.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

require "uri"

module HelpdeskConfig
  DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
  DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test"

  module_function

  def frontend_url
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].to_s.strip
    url = raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL : raw
    url.chomp("/")
  end

  def frontend_origin
    uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
    return frontend_url unless uri.scheme && uri.host

    origin = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"
    origin += ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port && uri.port != uri.default_port
    origin
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    frontend_url
  end

  def mail_from
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].to_s.strip
    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM : raw
  end
end

module HelpdeskConfig
  DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
  DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test"

  module_function

  def frontend_url
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].to_s.strip
    url = raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL : raw
    url.chomp("/")
  end

  def frontend_origin
    uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
    return frontend_url unless uri.scheme && uri.host

    origin = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"
    origin += ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port && uri.port != uri.default_port
    origin
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    frontend_url
  end

  def mail_from
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].to_s.strip
    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM : raw
  end
end

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  has_many :comments, dependent: :delete_all

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def self.open_request!(account:, requester:, subject:, comment_body:)
    now = Time.current
    ticket = new(
      account: account,
      requester: requester,
      subject: subject,
      status: "open",
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now
    )
    comment = Comment.new(
      account: account,
      ticket: ticket,
      author: requester,
      body: comment_body,
      public: true,
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now
    )

    ticket_valid = ticket.valid?
    comment_valid = comment.valid?

    unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        ticket.errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(ticket)
    end

    transaction do
      ticket.save!
      comment.ticket = ticket
      comment.save!
    end

    ticket
  end

  def apply_staff_update!(author:, has_comment:, comment_attrs:, has_status:, status:)
    unless has_comment || has_status
      errors.add(:base, "Comment or status is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    self.status = status if has_status
    comment = if has_comment
      Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: self,
        author: author,
        body: comment_attrs[:body],
        public: comment_attrs[:public]
      )
    end

    ticket_valid = valid?
    comment_valid = comment ? comment.valid? : true

    unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
      comment&.errors&.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    self.class.transaction do
      now = Time.current
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      end
      save!
    end

    self
  end

  def apply_customer_update!(author:, has_comment:, comment_body:, has_status:, status:)
    unless has_comment || has_status
      errors.add(:base, "Comment or status is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    errors.clear

    target_status = if has_status
      if status.blank?
        errors.add(:status, :blank)
        nil
      elsif status == "solved" || (has_comment && status == "open")
        status
      else
        errors.add(:status, :inclusion)
        nil
      end
    else
      "open"
    end

    comment = if has_comment
      Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: self,
        author: author,
        body: comment_body,
        public: true
      )
    end

    if comment && !comment.valid?
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
    end

    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self) if errors.any?

    self.class.transaction do
      now = Time.current
      self.status = target_status
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      end
      save!
    end

    self
  end

      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  has_many :comments, dependent: :delete_all

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def self.open_request!(account:, requester:, subject:, comment_body:)
    now = Time.current
    ticket = new(
      account: account,
      requester: requester,
      subject: subject,
      status: "open",
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now
    )
    comment = Comment.new(
      account: account,
      ticket: ticket,
      author: requester,
      body: comment_body,
      public: true,
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now
    )

    ticket_valid = ticket.valid?
    comment_valid = comment.valid?

    unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        ticket.errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(ticket)
    end

    transaction do
      ticket.save!
      comment.ticket = ticket
      comment.save!
    end

    ticket
  end

  def apply_staff_update!(author:, has_comment:, comment_attrs:, has_status:, status:)
    unless has_comment || has_status
      errors.add(:base, "Comment or status is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    self.status = status if has_status
    comment = if has_comment
      Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: self,
        author: author,
        body: comment_attrs[:body],
        public: comment_attrs[:public]
      )
    end

    ticket_valid = valid?
    comment_valid = comment ? comment.valid? : true

    unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
      comment&.errors&.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    self.class.transaction do
      now = Time.current
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      end
      save!
    end

    self
  end

  def apply_customer_update!(author:, has_comment:, comment_body:, has_status:, status:)
    unless has_comment || has_status
      errors.add(:base, "Comment or status is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    errors.clear

    target_status = if has_status
      if status.blank?
        errors.add(:status, :blank)
        nil
      elsif status == "solved" || (has_comment && status == "open")
        status
      else
        errors.add(:status, :inclusion)
        nil
      end
    else
      "open"
    end

    comment = if has_comment
      Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: self,
        author: author,
        body: comment_body,
        public: true
      )
    end

    if comment && !comment.valid?
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
    end

    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self) if errors.any?

    self.class.transaction do
      now = Time.current
      self.status = target_status
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      end
      save!
    end

    self
  end

      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at

class User < ApplicationRecord
  ROLES = %w[admin agent customer].freeze
  STAFF_ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  has_many :requested_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :requester_id, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :comments, foreign_key: :author_id, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :email_verification_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :password_reset_tokens, dependent: :delete_all

  has_secure_password

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }
  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip.downcase : value }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP },
    uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }
  validates :password, length: { minimum: 6 }, if: -> { password.present? }

  def account_owner?
    account.owner_id == id
  end

  def staff?
    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"
  end

  def issue_email_verification_token!
    transaction do
      email_verification_tokens.delete_all
      EmailVerificationToken.issue_for!(self)
    end
  end

  def issue_password_reset_token!
    transaction do
      password_reset_tokens.delete_all
      PasswordResetToken.issue_for!(self)
    end
  end

  def verify_email!
    transaction do
      update!(verified: true, email_verified_at: email_verified_at || Time.current)
      email_verification_tokens.delete_all
    end
  end

  def change_password!(new_password)
    unless new_password.is_a?(String) && new_password.present?
      errors.add(:password, :blank)
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    transaction do
      self.password = new_password
      save!
      sessions.delete_all
      password_reset_tokens.delete_all
    end
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      account_id: account_id,
      name: name,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      verified: verified,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end
end

        return default unless parsed && parsed >= 1

require "test_helper"

class EdgeCasesTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  def json_body
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def extract_token(mail)
    uri = URI.parse(mail.body.decoded[%r{https?://[^\s"<>]+}])
    URI.decode_www_form(uri.query).to_h.fetch("token")
  end

  test "expired verification and password reset tokens are rejected" do
    post "/api/v1/account/create",
      params: {
        account: {
          name: "Acme",
          subdomain: "acme",
          admin: { name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password" }
        }
      },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    verify_token = extract_token(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last)

    travel 49.hours do
      post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
        params: { email_verification: { token: verify_token } },
        headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
        as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end

It seems to currently return a JSON representation of a request with these attributes: `id`, `subject`, `status`, `requester_id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. Here's where the problem arises: Currently, the `tickets` table seems to have a single `updated_at` column. So, whenever staff adds a private note or assigns a ticket, the `ticket.updated_at` gets updated via ActiveRecord's `save!` method.

    assert json_body.dig("account", "cancelled_at").present?

    # Existing sessions for both owner and Sam are revoked
    get "/api/v1/me", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{owner_token}" }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    get "/api/v1/me", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{sam_token}" }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    # Ordinary business access is stopped (public portal, password reset, non-owner login)
    get "/api/v1/portal", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" }
    assert_response :forbidden

    post "/api/v1/sessions",
      params: { session: { email: "sam@acme.test", password: "sam-password" } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden

    # Owner can still sign in while cancelled within 90 days
    travel 89.days do
      owner_recovery_login = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
      recovery_token = owner_recovery_login.dig("session", "token")
      assert owner_recovery_login.dig("account", "cancelled_at").present?

      # Ordinary endpoints remain blocked until reactivated
      get "/api/v1/account", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{recovery_token}" }
      assert_response :forbidden

      get "/api/v1/me", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{recovery_token}" }
      assert_response :forbidden

      # Purge task does NOT delete accounts cancelled < 90 days ago
      Account.purge_cancelled!
      assert Account.exists?(acme.id)

      # Owner reactivates the account
      post "/api/v1/account/reactivate", headers: {
        "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme",
        "Authorization" => "Bearer #{recovery_token}"
      }
      assert_response :ok
      assert_nil json_body.dig("account", "cancelled_at")

      # Ordinary business access works again
      get "/api/v1/portal", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" }
      assert_response :ok

      get "/api/v1/account", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{recovery_token}" }
      assert_response :ok

      get "/api/v1/me", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{recovery_token}" }
      assert_response :ok

      sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@acme.test", password: "sam-password")
    end

    # Cancel again and test expiration + rake task purge after 90 days
    register_and_verify!(subdomain: "keepme", name: "KeepMe", email: "jo@keepme.test")
    keepme = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "keepme")

    fresh_owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password").dig("session", "token")
    post "/api/v1/account/cancel", headers: {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme",
      "Authorization" => "Bearer #{fresh_owner_token}"
    }
    assert_response :ok

    # Create tokens on acme to verify all child records are purged too
    second_admin.issue_password_reset_token!
    second_admin.issue_email_verification_token!

    Rails.application.load_tasks if Rake::Task.tasks.empty?

    travel 90.days + 1.second do
      # Past 90 days: owner cannot sign in to reactivate anymore
      post "/api/v1/sessions",
        params: { session: { email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password" } },
        headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
        as: :json
      assert_response :forbidden

      Rake::Task["helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts"].reenable
      Rake::Task["helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts"].invoke

      assert_not Account.exists?(acme.id)
      assert_equal 0, User.where(account_id: acme.id).count
      assert_equal 0, Session.where(account_id: acme.id).count
      assert_equal 0, EmailVerificationToken.where(account_id: acme.id).count
      assert_equal 0, PasswordResetToken.where(account_id: acme.id).count

      # Active account is untouched
      assert Account.exists?(keepme.id)
      assert_equal 1, User.where(account_id: keepme.id).count
    end
  end
end

The test's posting to `/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm` with the "globex" token and the `X-Helpdesk-Account: acme` header, and it's resulting in an `unprocessable_content` response. messages.thinking:
**Invitation Design Deep Dive**

Okay, so I've got this invitation system to design, and it's looking like a central piece of the application's admin functionality. Here's how I see it all breaking down:

The core is `X-Helpdesk-Account` consistency, which permeates all tenant-scoped endpoints, just like the invitation email URL and other account-related URLs. The way `X-Helpdesk-Account` is validated and tied into the token is rock-solid, forming the base of authorization.

Now, let's drill down into each detail of the `Invitation` component:

1.  **Authorization:** Admins and only admins are in charge. The `before_action` filters are critical: `authenticate_user!`, `require_active_account!`, and `require_admin!`. Active admins can handle users, but account cancellation/reactivation requires the owner, and those suspended don't get through authentication.

2.  **Roles:** Only `"admin"` and `"agent"` are allowed; validation is paramount (`validates :role`). Role validation, like ticket status validation, needs exact matching, ensuring no ambiguity and proper error handling with `422 Unprocessable Content`.

3.  **Email Validation:** Just like user email, email normalization (strip, downcase) and validation are crucial.

4.  **Conflict Prevention:** This is critical! I need to ensure that the system handles every possible conflict scenario:
    *   **Existing User:** No invite if an email is already in the account. That would error with a `422 Unprocessable Content`.
    *   **Pending Invitation:** No duplicate pending invitations for the same email. This is essential for preventing confusion and ensuring the system is consistent! The best way is to `account.with_lock` within a transaction to avoid race conditions. An expired invitation can be re-sent.
    *   **Multi-Tenancy:** Each account operates in its own silo, and invitations are scoped to the account.
    *   **Customer Registration:** If there's a pending invitation, registration fails until the invite is accepted, revoked, or expired.
    *   **Customer Prior to Invite:** If a user registers before an invite, the invite will fail.
    *   **Database/Transaction:** I need to make sure that the database level validates and enforces all constraints.

5.  **Status and Lifecycle:** This is where the magic happens! I need to make sure I am modeling invitations correctly:
    *   I'll track `id`, `account_id`, `invited_by_id`, `email`, `role`, `token_digest`, `expires_at`, `accepted_at`, `revoked_at`, and `created_at` / `updated_at`.
    *   Status is derived from timestamps: `"pending"`, `"accepted"`, `"revoked"`, `"expired"`. This will mean that a single DB row is always in an exact, valid state, and is easily filtered with SQL `WHERE` clauses.

6.  **TTL (Time-To-Live):** Standard is 7 days, based on best practices and the prompt. Expiry is returned in the JSON response, so it needs to be calculated.

7.  **Resend Action:**
    *   Can Be Called By: an admin.
    *   When an invitation is resent, it will generate a new token and update both `token_digest` and `expires_at`. The action must return a JSON response with the current invitation details with status `:ok`.
    *   Resend conditions:
        *   Pending: YES - action succeeds, generates a new token and refreshes `expires_at`.
        *   Accepted: NO - action fails.
        *   Revoked: NO - action fails.
        *   Expired: YES - The key question! Because the prompt allows resending to an expired invite, as long as it isn't blocked by the other rules, the re-sent invitation will have a new token with a new expiry, and status `"pending"`.
        *   The conflict checks (`ensure_no_competing_user_or_pending_invitation!`) must happen to avoid a race condition.

8.  **Revoke Action:**
    *   Revoking does **not** destroy the row but sets the `revoked_at` timestamp.
    *   The `DELETE` verb is used.
    *   Return code: I will need to return `200 OK` with the `invitation` payload (status, etc.), making it clear that the invitation has been revoked. This allows me to easily track revoked invitations.

**Deep Dive into Invitation Management in this Helpdesk API**

Okay, here's the breakdown of my thought process, as an expert in this codebase, regarding these invitation endpoints. I'm focusing on the subtle design choices and ensuring consistency with the existing patterns.

First, I had to clarify the intent behind the `DELETE /api/v1/invitations/:id` action. Why "revoke" instead of "delete"? Looking at the prompt and the existing API design (Stripe, GitHub, the whole vibe), a `DELETE` on a resource that can be "revoked" is a soft-delete, a cancellation, a revocation, which *explicitly* keeps the audit trail and state transition. This directly aligns with how `POST /api/v1/account/cancel` works and what's expected in the prompt. I know, from experience with this codebase, that `DELETE /api/v1/session` is destructive because it deletes the record. This is different!

Next, the frontend implications. If the admin clicks "Revoke", does the frontend get the updated object? Yes. If we return `200 OK` with the updated JSON, we're consistent with `POST /invitations/:id/resend`, `POST /account/cancel`, and `PATCH /users/:id`. Plus, it means tests are easy to write. I know we already have those test conventions. Returning `200 OK` is standard REST with an updated resource.

Now, let's look at the patterns in the coding style. We *always* return JSON responses. Literally, every single endpoint in `api/v1/` returns JSON with `{ <resource>: ... }` (except when the action truly destroys the record). Even the "status ok" endpoints return `{ <resource>: { status: "ok" } }`. So, `DELETE /invitations/:id` returning `{ invitation: ... }` is *exactly* what this codebase does. It's consistent with `AccountsController#cancel` soft-cancelling the account, `InvitationsController#destroy` soft-revokes the invitation. I also need to make sure we handle the different statuses correctly. `expired` invitations? `422`. Always.

Then, I meticulously examined the behavior of `POST /invitations/:id/resend`. The key is to handle edge cases in a sensible way. If the invitation is "pending", resend is good. If the invite has expired, and the email is still free, resend it with a new token (as the user would expect). This is *not* a delete, so it should not be a problem. This is exactly what the prompt wants.

Finally, the JSON structure! The prompt's emphasis on "email, role, business name, subdomain, and expiry inside `invitation_preview`" is key. Now, it's vital to maintain consistency within our API. Remember `helpdesk_api_test.rb`? This is *where* to get this right. The existing style is to provide an *exact* hash response when returning portal information.

Therefore:

1.  Invitation JSON (`as_api_json`):
    -   `id`, `account_id`, `email`, `role`, `status`, `invited_by_id`, `expires_at`, `accepted_at`, `revoked_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Never `token` or `token_digest`. `invited_by_id` fits the pattern of other IDs.

2.  Email (the user needs the link in the email):
    -   Link to the frontend like this: `http://localhost:3001/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=abc...`

3.  Listing and inspecting invitations (`GET` endpoints):
    -   Paging and ordering are as usual: paging, with `count`, `page`, `per_page`, etc. Ordering by `id: :asc`. Filtering, but treat invalid status filtering as `422 Unprocessable Content`.

4.  `POST /invitation_previews` : The acceptance screen!
    -   Crucially, I need to look at **every existing serializer**.

    -   The return for `invitation_preview` should have a very specific structure. Remember the other calls like `portal` (where we ONLY return `name` and `subdomain`) and the format of the `account` nested.

    -   The key names will be:
        -   `email`, `role`, `expires_at`
        -   `account`: `{ "name": "Acme", "subdomain": "acme" }`. This is the most consistent and correct approach, aligning with the `Account` object.

**Comprehensive Review of Ticket Assignment, User Management, and Security Considerations**

Alright, let's break this down. The first thing that jumps out is the elegance of using `account: account.as_portal_json` in the invitation preview. It's clean and keeps the public information in a nested structure. That's a solid win. The prompt's focus on what's *inside* the `invitation_preview` is important, because we need to be very clear which keys get returned in the JSON. The presence of both the nested `account` and the flat `account_name` and `subdomain` is safe. There are no private fields present in that object, so that's all good. I can confidently say that this approach covers all bases.

Moving onto user acceptance, the endpoint `POST /invitation_acceptances` has all the right checks. The logic around token validation, user creation, role assignment, and atomic updates (using `with_lock`) is robust. The 201 Created response for new resource creation also matches REST conventions.

Next up, user management (`GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, `PATCH /users/:id`) with the `suspended` field. We need to implement the database column, ensure it's in the API response, and handle the logic around user suspension. Suspension revokes sessions, clears assignments, which is all standard practice. The "last active admin" rule is critical. The requirement to validate an `assignee_id` is the key.

The edge case with the last active admin is clear: you can't suspend the only active admin. Suspension revokes sessions and clears ticket assignments. Good. The handling of the database column for `suspended` is also well-defined with default `false`. The goal is to always leave at least one active admin, and the code needs to ensure that.

Now, we need to think about `GET /staff` and `GET /users` separation. "Staff can assign tickets ... BOTH admins AND agents", so agents need access to assignment controls without all user management privileges of admins. I am comfortable with this separation and the need for a staff-focused endpoint for assigning tickets.

For ticket assignment, we validate the `assignee_id` very carefully. Handling nil, valid staff users, and invalid IDs with proper 422 errors and atomic transaction rollbacks are all important. Validating staff roles, account membership, and suspension is a good approach. The ability to update ticket assignments alongside comments and status changes is great, but we want to make sure it's valid.

Regarding customer visibility, the introduction of `customer_updated_at` is brilliant. This preserves the customer-facing view from irrelevant staff activity. Public comments update `customer_updated_at`. Internal changes like assigning a ticket, or a private comment, do *not* impact this timestamp. This has important consequences for comment updates, status changes, etc.

I'm confident we have a solid solution here.

Let's do a quick double-check: account purging, account cancellation, and role separation are correctly handled. The staff/role access is clean. Role-based authorization also prevents role escalation from customers to admin. Suspending users clears ticket assignments.

require "digest"

class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 7.days
  ROLES = User::STAFF_ROLES
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip.downcase : value }

  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }
  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true

  scope :ordered, -> { order(id: :asc) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :expired, ->(now = Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at <= ?", now) }
  scope :pending, ->(now = Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at > ?", now) }

  def self.with_status(status, now = Time.current)
    case status
    when "pending" then pending(now)
    when "accepted" then accepted
    when "revoked" then revoked
    when "expired" then expired(now)
    else none
    end
  end

  def self.digest(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
  end

  def self.find_valid_for_account(account, raw_token)
    return nil unless account && raw_token.is_a?(String) && raw_token.present?

    account.invitations
      .includes(:account)
      .pending
      .find_by(token_digest: digest(raw_token))
  end

  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:)
    raw_token = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(40)
    invitation = account.invitations.new(
      invited_by: invited_by,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      token_digest: digest(raw_token),
      expires_at: TTL.from_now
    )

    account.with_lock do
      valid = invitation.valid?
      if invitation.email.present? && !invitation.errors.include?(:email)
        if account.users.exists?(email: invitation.email) || account.invitations.pending.exists?(email: invitation.email)
          invitation.errors.add(:email, :taken)
          valid = false
        end
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(invitation) unless valid

      invitation.save!
    end

    UserMailer.invitation(invitation, raw_token).deliver_now

    invitation
  end

  def self.accept_for_account!(account:, raw_token:, name:, password:)
    return nil unless account && raw_token.is_a?(String) && raw_token.present?

    account.with_lock do
      invitation = account.invitations.pending.find_by(token_digest: digest(raw_token))
      return nil if invitation.nil?

      now = Time.current
      user = account.users.new(
        name: name,
        email: invitation.email,
        role: invitation.role,
        verified: true,
        email_verified_at: now,
        suspended: false
      )
      user.password = password if password.is_a?(String) && password.present?
      user.save!

      invitation.update!(accepted_at: now)
      user
    end
  end

  def status(now = Time.current)
    if accepted_at.present?
      "accepted"
    elsif revoked_at.present?
      "revoked"
    elsif expires_at <= now
      "expired"
    else
      "pending"
    end
  end

  def accepted?
    accepted_at.present?
  end

  def revoked?
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.present?
  end

  def expired?(now = Time.current)
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.nil? && expires_at <= now
  end

  def pending?(now = Time.current)
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.nil? && expires_at > now
  end

  def resend!
    raw_token = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(40)

    account.with_lock do
      reload
      if accepted?
        errors.add(:base, "Invitation has already been accepted")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      if revoked?
        errors.add(:base, "Invitation has been revoked")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      if account.users.exists?(email: email) || account.invitations.pending.where.not(id: id).exists?(email: email)
        errors.add(:email, :taken)
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      update!(
        token_digest: self.class.digest(raw_token),
        expires_at: TTL.from_now
      )
    end

    UserMailer.invitation(self, raw_token).deliver_now
    self
  end

  def revoke!
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      if accepted?
        errors.add(:base, "Invitation has already been accepted")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      if revoked?
        errors.add(:base, "Invitation has already been revoked")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      if expired?
        errors.add(:base, "Invitation has already expired")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      update!(revoked_at: Time.current)
    end

    self
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_id: invited_by_id,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      status: status,
      expires_at: expires_at,
      accepted_at: accepted_at,
      revoked_at: revoked_at,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  def as_preview_json
    {
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account: account.as_portal_json,
      account_name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain,
      expires_at: expires_at
    }
  end
end
EOF

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD = 90.days
  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/

  belongs_to :owner, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :email_verification_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :password_reset_tokens, dependent: :delete_all

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip.downcase : value }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :subdomain,
    presence: true,
    uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false },
    format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT }

  scope :purge_eligible, -> {
    where.not(cancelled_at: nil).where(cancelled_at: ..CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD.ago)
  }

  def self.register!(account_attrs:, admin_attrs:)
    account = new(
      name: account_attrs[:name],
      subdomain: account_attrs[:subdomain]
    )
    user = User.new(
      account: account,
      name: admin_attrs[:name],
      email: admin_attrs[:email],
      role: "admin",
      verified: false
    )
    raw_password = admin_attrs[:password]
    user.password = raw_password if raw_password.is_a?(String) && raw_password.present?

    account_valid = account.valid?
    user_valid = user.valid?

    unless account_valid && user_valid
      user.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :account
        account.errors.add(:"admin.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(account)
    end

    raw_verification_token = nil

    transaction do
      account.save!
      user.account = account
      user.save!
      account.update!(owner: user)
      raw_verification_token = user.issue_email_verification_token!\
    end

    UserMailer.email_verification(user, raw_verification_token).deliver_now

    [account, user]
  end

  def self.purge_cancelled!
    count = 0
    purge_eligible.find_each do |account|
      account.purge!
      count += 1
    end
    count
  end

  def register_customer!(attrs)
    user = users.new(
      name: attrs[:name],
      email: attrs[:email],
      role: "customer",
      verified: false
    )
    raw_password = attrs[:password]
    user.password = raw_password if raw_password.is_a?(String) && raw_password.present?

    raw_verification_token = nil

    with_lock do
      valid = user.valid?
      if user.email.present? && !user.errors.include?(:email) && invitations.pending.exists?(email: user.email)
        user.errors.add(:email, :taken)
        valid = false
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(user) unless valid

      user.save!
      raw_verification_token = user.issue_email_verification_token!
    end

    UserMailer.email_verification(user, raw_verification_token).deliver_now

    user
  end

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def reactivable?
    cancelled? && cancelled_at > CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD.ago
  end

  def cancel!
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: Time.current)
      sessions.delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: nil)
    end
  end

  def purge!
    transaction do
      update_columns(owner_id: nil)
      destroy!
    end
  end

  def as_portal_json
    {
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain
    }
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      owner_id: owner_id,

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  MAX_BIGINT = (1 << 63) - 1

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, dependent: :delete_all

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }

  before_create :ensure_customer_updated_at

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :customer_recently_active, -> { order(customer_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def self.open_request!(account:, requester:, subject:, comment_body:)
    now = Time.current
    ticket = new(
      account: account,
      requester: requester,
      subject: subject,
      status: "open",
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now,
      customer_updated_at: now
    )
    comment = Comment.new(
      account: account,
      ticket: ticket,
      author: requester,
      body: comment_body,
      public: true,
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now
    )

    ticket_valid = ticket.valid?
    comment_valid = comment.valid?

    unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        ticket.errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(ticket)
    end

    transaction do
      ticket.save!
      comment.ticket = ticket
      comment.save!
    end

    ticket
  end

  def apply_staff_update!(author:, has_comment:, comment_attrs:, has_status:, status:, has_assignee: false, raw_assignee_id: nil)
    unless has_comment || has_status || has_assignee
      errors.add(:base, "Comment, status, or assignee is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    self.status = status if has_status

    assignee_invalid = false
    if has_assignee
      if raw_assignee_id.nil?
        self.assignee = nil
      else
        parsed_id = parse_assignee_id(raw_assignee_id)
        staff_member = parsed_id && account.users.active_staff.find_by(id: parsed_id)
        if staff_member
          self.assignee = staff_member
        else
          assignee_invalid = true
        end
      end
    end

    comment = if has_comment
      Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: self,
        author: author,
        body: comment_attrs[:body],
        public: comment_attrs[:public]
      )
    end

    ticket_valid = valid?
    if assignee_invalid
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "is invalid")
      ticket_valid = false
    end
    comment_valid = comment ? comment.valid? : true

    unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
      comment&.errors&.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    customer_visible_change = (comment.present? && comment.public?) || will_save_change_to_status?

    self.class.transaction do
      now = Time.current
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      elsif will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id?
        self.updated_at = now
      end

      self.customer_updated_at = now if customer_visible_change
      save!
    end

    self
  end

  def apply_customer_update!(author:, has_comment:, comment_body:, has_status:, status:)
    unless has_comment || has_status
      errors.add(:base, "Comment or status is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    errors.clear

    target_status = if has_status
      if status.blank?
        errors.add(:status, :blank)
        nil
      elsif status == "solved" || (has_comment && status == "open")
        status
      else
        errors.add(:status, :inclusion)
        nil
      end
    else
      "open"
    end

    comment = if has_comment
      Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: self,
        author: author,
        body: comment_body,
        public: true
      )
    end

    if comment && !comment.valid?
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
    end

    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self) if errors.any?

    self.class.transaction do
      now = Time.current
      self.status = target_status
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      elsif will_save_change_to_status?
        self.updated_at = now
      end
      self.customer_updated_at = now if comment || will_save_change_to_status?
      save!
    end

    self
  end

  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: customer_updated_at
    }
  end

  def as_ticket_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      requester: {
        id: requester.id,
        name: requester.name,
        email: requester.email
      },
      assignee_id: assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee ? {
        id: assignee.id,
        name: assignee.name
      } : nil,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def ensure_customer_updated_at
    self.customer_updated_at ||= updated_at || created_at || Time.current
  end

  def parse_assignee_id(raw_id)
    return nil unless raw_id.is_a?(Integer) || raw_id.is_a?(String)

    id = Integer(raw_id.to_s, 10, exception: false)
    return nil unless id && id >= 1 && id <= MAX_BIGINT

    id
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      BEARER_PATTERN = /\ABearer\s+(\S+)\s*\z/i
      MAX_BIGINT = (1 << 63) - 1
      DEFAULT_PAGE = 1
      DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
      MAX_PER_PAGE = 1000
      MAX_PAGE = 1_000_000_000

      before_action :set_current_account!

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing, with: :render_parameter_missing
      rescue_from ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError, with: :render_parse_error
      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, with: :render_record_invalid
      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, with: :render_record_not_unique

      private

      attr_reader :current_account, :current_user, :current_session

      def set_current_account!
        raw_header = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"]
        subdomain = raw_header.is_a?(String) ? raw_header.strip.downcase : ""

        if subdomain.empty?
          render json: { error: "X-Helpdesk-Account header is required" }, status: :bad_request
          return
        end

        @current_account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
        return if @current_account

        render json: { error: "Account not found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      def authenticate_user!
        raw_token = extract_bearer_token
        @current_session = Session.find_for_account_by_token(current_account, raw_token)

        if @current_session.nil? || @current_session.user.suspended?
          render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
          return
        end

        @current_user = @current_session.user
      end

      def require_active_account!
        return if current_account&.active?

        render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_account_owner!
        return if current_user&.account_owner?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_admin!
        return if current_user&.admin?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_staff!
        return if current_user&.staff?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_customer!
        return if current_user&.customer?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def extract_bearer_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"]
        return nil unless header.is_a?(String)

        match = BEARER_PATTERN.match(header.strip)
        match && match[1]
      end

      def require_object_param(key, source = params)
        value = source[key]
        raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, key unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

        value
      end

      def scalar_string(value)
        value.is_a?(String) ? value : nil
      end

      def extract_boolean_param(params_obj, key, default:)
        return default unless params_obj.key?(key)

        value = params_obj[key]
        (value == true || value == false) ? value : nil
      end

      def extract_query_boolean(raw_value)
        if raw_value == true || raw_value == "true"
          true
        elsif raw_value == false || raw_value == "false"
          false
        else
          :invalid
        end
      end

      def parse_record_id(raw_id)
        return nil unless raw_id.is_a?(String) || raw_id.is_a?(Integer)

        id = Integer(raw_id.to_s, 10, exception: false)
        return nil unless id && id >= 1 && id <= MAX_BIGINT

        id
      end

      def parse_pagination_param(raw_value, default:, max:)
        return default unless raw_value.is_a?(String) || raw_value.is_a?(Integer)

        parsed = Integer(raw_value.to_s.strip, 10, exception: false)
        return default unless parsed && parsed >= 1

        [parsed, max].min
      end

      def paginate(scope, resource_key:, &serializer)
        page = parse_pagination_param(params[:page], default: DEFAULT_PAGE, max: MAX_PAGE)
        per_page = parse_pagination_param(params[:per_page], default: DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, max: MAX_PER_PAGE)
        total_count = scope.count
        offset = (page - 1) * per_page

        records = if offset >= total_count
          []
        else
          scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).map(&serializer)
        end

        {
          resource_key => records,
          count: total_count,
          page: page,
          per_page: per_page,
          next_page: (page * per_page < total_count) ? page + 1 : nil,
          previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
        }
      end

      def render_parameter_missing(exception)
        render json: { error: exception.message }, status: :bad_request
      end

      def render_parse_error(_exception)
        render json: { error: "Invalid JSON payload" }, status: :bad_request
      end

      def render_record_invalid(exception)
        errors_hash = exception.record.errors.to_hash(true)
        render json: {
          error: exception.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence,
          errors: errors_hash
        }, status: :unprocessable_content
      end

      def render_record_not_unique(_exception)
        render json: { error: "Record already exists" }, status: :unprocessable_content
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

        email = scalar_string(session_params[:email])

          current_account.users.authenticate_by(email: email, password: password)

          render json: { error: "Invalid email or password" }, status: :unauthorized

        unless user.verified?
          render json: { error: "Email must be verified before signing in" }, status: :forbidden

        if user.suspended?
          render json: { error: "User is suspended" }, status: :forbidden

        if current_account.cancelled? && !(user.account_owner? && current_account.reactivable?)
          render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
          return
        end

        render json: {
          session: session_record.as_api_json,
          user: user.as_api_json,
          account: current_account.as_api_json
        }, status: :created
      end

      def destroy
        current_session.destroy!
        head :no_content
      end
    end
  end

module Api
  module V1
    class PasswordResetsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def create
        pr_params = require_object_param(:password_reset)
        email = scalar_string(pr_params[:email]).to_s.strip.downcase

        if email.empty?
          render json: {
            error: "Email can't be blank",
            errors: { email: ["can't be blank"] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_content
          return
        end

        user = current_account.users.find_by(email: email)
        if user && !user.suspended?
          raw_token = user.issue_password_reset_token!
          UserMailer.password_reset(user, raw_token).deliver_now
        end

        render json: { password_reset: { status: "ok" } }, status: :ok
      end

      def confirm
        pr_params = require_object_param(:password_reset)
        raw_token = scalar_string(pr_params[:token])
        new_password = scalar_string(pr_params[:password])
        token_record = PasswordResetToken.find_valid_for_account(current_account, raw_token)

          render json: {
            error: "Invalid or expired password reset token",
            errors: { token: ["is invalid or expired"] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_content
          return
        end

        user = token_record.user
        user.change_password!(new_password)

        render json: { user: user.as_api_json }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"
require "rake"

class TeamAndCollaborationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    ENV.delete("HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL")
    ENV.delete("HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM")
  end

  def json_body
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def extract_link_params(mail, expected_path)
    body = mail.body.decoded
    match = body.match(%r{(https?://[^\s"<>]+)})
    assert match, "Expected URL in email body, got: #{body.inspect}"
    uri = URI.parse(match[1])
    assert_equal expected_path, uri.path
    [uri, URI.decode_www_form(uri.query).to_h]
  end

  def setup_business!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    post "/api/v1/account/create",
      params: {
        account: {
          name: name,
          subdomain: subdomain,
          admin: { name: admin_name, email: email, password: password }
        }
      },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    owner = json_body.fetch("user")
    _uri, query = extract_link_params(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/verify-email")

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: query.fetch("token") } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    owner
  end

  def register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
      params: { user: { name: name, email: email, password: password } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    _uri, query = extract_link_params(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/verify-email")

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: query.fetch("token") } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    user = json_body.fetch("user")
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    user
  end

  def sign_in!(subdomain:, email:, password:)
    post "/api/v1/sessions",
      params: { session: { email: email, password: password } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    json_body.dig("session", "token")
  end

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)
    {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}"
    }
  end

  test "invitation lifecycle: create, preview, accept, resend, revoke, expire, filter, ID asc order, and competing email rules" do
    setup_business!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test")
    owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    owner_headers = auth_headers("acme", owner_token)

    # Admin invites Sam as agent
    assert_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }, 1 do
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
        params: { invitation: { email: "  SAM@Example.Test ", role: "agent" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
    end
    assert_response :created

    sam_invite = json_body.fetch("invitation")
    assert_kind_of Integer, sam_invite["id"]
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", sam_invite["email"]
    assert_equal "agent", sam_invite["role"]
    assert_equal "pending", sam_invite["status"]
    assert sam_invite["expires_at"].present?
    assert_nil sam_invite["accepted_at"]
    assert_nil sam_invite["revoked_at"]
    assert_not sam_invite.key?("token")
    assert_not sam_invite.key?("token_digest")

    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_equal ["sam@example.test"], mail.to
    uri, query = extract_link_params(mail, "/accept-invitation")
    assert_equal "http://localhost:3001", "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}:#{uri.port}"
    assert_equal "acme", query["account"]
    first_sam_token = query.fetch("token")
    assert first_sam_token.present?

    # Competing pending invitation for same email is rejected and sends no email
    assert_no_difference [-> { Invitation.count }, -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }] do
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
        params: { invitation: { email: "sam@example.test", role: "admin" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end

    # Cannot invite an already existing user's email
    assert_no_difference [-> { Invitation.count }, -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }] do
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
        params: { invitation: { email: "JO@ACME.TEST", role: "agent" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end

    # Invalid role (e.g. customer) cannot be invited
    assert_no_difference [-> { Invitation.count }, -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }] do
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
        params: { invitation: { email: "cust@example.test", role: "customer" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end

    # Customer registration cannot take a pending invite's email
    assert_no_difference [-> { User.count }, -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }] do
      post "/api/v1/registrations",
        params: { user: { name: "Sam Customer", email: "SAM@example.test", password: "customer-password" } },
        headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
        as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end

    # Resend rotates token and refreshes expiry
    travel 1.hour do
      assert_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }, 1 do
        post "/api/v1/invitations/#{sam_invite["id"]}/resend", headers: owner_headers
      end
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal "pending", json_body.dig("invitation", "status")
      assert_operator Time.iso8601(json_body.dig("invitation", "expires_at")), :>, Time.iso8601(sam_invite["expires_at"])
    end

    _uri2, query2 = extract_link_params(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/accept-invitation")
    resent_sam_token = query2.fetch("token")
    assert_not_equal first_sam_token, resent_sam_token

    # Old token is invalidated on both preview and acceptance
    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
      params: { invitation_preview: { token: first_sam_token } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
      params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: first_sam_token, name: "Sam", password: "my-team-password" } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    # Preview with valid resent token shows invited email, role, business name, subdomain, and expiry
    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
      params: { invitation_preview: { token: resent_sam_token } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    preview = json_body.fetch("invitation_preview")
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", preview["email"]
    assert_equal "agent", preview["role"]
    assert_equal({ "name" => "Acme", "subdomain" => "acme" }, preview["account"])
    assert_equal "Acme", preview["account_name"]
    assert_equal "acme", preview["subdomain"]
    assert preview["expires_at"].present?
    assert_not preview.key?("token")
    assert_not preview.key?("token_digest")

    # Invalid acceptance form input (short password / blank name) rolls back and keeps invitation pending
    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
        params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: resent_sam_token, name: "   ", password: "short" } },
        headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
        as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end

    # Accept invitation: returns user and account, sends NO verification email, Sam can immediately sign in
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    assert_no_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size } do
      post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
        params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: resent_sam_token, name: " Sam ", password: "my-team-password" } },
        headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
        as: :json
    end
    assert_response :created

    sam_user = json_body.fetch("user")
    accepted_account = json_body.fetch("account")
    assert_equal "Sam", sam_user["name"]
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", sam_user["email"]
    assert_equal "agent", sam_user["role"]
    assert_equal true, sam_user["verified"]
    assert_equal false, sam_user["suspended"]
    assert_equal "acme", accepted_account["subdomain"]

    # Sam signs in immediately without another verification email
    sam_session_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@example.test", password: "my-team-password")
    assert sam_session_token.present?

    # Accepted invitation cannot be previewed, accepted again, resent, or revoked
    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
      params: { invitation_preview: { token: resent_sam_token } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
      params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: resent_sam_token, name: "Sam 2", password: "my-team-password" } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    post "/api/v1/invitations/#{sam_invite["id"]}/resend", headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{sam_invite["id"]}", headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    # Create 3 more invitations to test revoked, expired, and pending statuses + ID ascending + status filters
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
      params: { invitation: { email: "revoked@example.test", role: "agent" } },
      headers: owner_headers,
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    revoked_invite_id = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
    _u, revoked_q = extract_link_params(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/accept-invitation")

    delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{revoked_invite_id}", headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "revoked", json_body.dig("invitation", "status")
    assert json_body.dig("invitation", "revoked_at").present?

    # Double revoke and resend of revoked invite fail; token no longer works
    delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{revoked_invite_id}", headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    post "/api/v1/invitations/#{revoked_invite_id}/resend", headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
      params: { invitation_preview: { token: revoked_q["token"] } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    # Customer registration CAN take a revoked invite's email

    travel 8.days do
      # Expired token fails preview and acceptance

        as: :json
      claimer_headers = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{json_body.dig("session", "token")}" }

      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Edge ticket", comment: { body: "Edge body" } } },
        headers: claimer_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :created
      ticket_id = json_body.dig("request", "id")
      req_before = json_body.fetch("request")

      [true, false, 0, -5, ["arr"], { bad: 1 }, 99_999_999_999_999_999_999_999_999].each do |bad_assignee|
        patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
          params: { ticket: { assignee_id: bad_assignee } },
          headers: owner_headers,
          as: :json
        assert_response :unprocessable_content
      end

      ["not-bool", nil, ["arr"]].each do |bad_public|
        patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
          params: { ticket: { comment: { body: "Note", public: bad_public } } },
          headers: owner_headers,
          as: :json
        assert_response :unprocessable_content
      end

      # Passing same status ("open") alongside private note still does not change customer-facing request
      travel 3.minutes do
        patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
          params: { ticket: { comment: { body: "Private note with unchanged status", public: false }, status: "open" } },
          headers: owner_headers,
          as: :json
        assert_response :ok
      end

      get "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}", headers: claimer_headers
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal req_before, json_body.fetch("request")
    end
  end
end

messages.thinking:
**Critical Security and Design Considerations**

Okay, hold on a second! Before we proceed, I need to address a crucial question. What happens if the frontend's acceptance screen (`/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN`) or an automated test calls either `POST /api/v1/invitation_previews` or `POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances` *without* the `X-Helpdesk-Account` header? We need to really think this through. Let's break down the implications...

1.  **Scenario with the `X-Helpdesk-Account` header:**

    *   If the header *is* present, we have defined behaviours which are correct, returning the appropriate 404, 403, 422, or 200/201 responses based on the account's validity and the token's relationship to the account. This all makes sense.

2.  **Scenario *without* the `X-Helpdesk-Account` header:**

    This is where things get interesting, and potentially problematic. Thinking back to the prompt, we see that it states: "to show the invited email, role, business name, subdomain, and expiry inside `invitation_preview`" *and* "Return `user` and `account`". The frontend, as it's designed, *already* knows the `account` from the URL parameter, `?account=acme` in `/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN`, and will send the `X-Helpdesk-Account: acme` in the request. But, what if someone bypasses this designed flow?

    This raises significant questions: What if someone *only* has the token, or they're deliberately testing missing the `X-Helpdesk-Account` header, expecting a `400 Bad Request`? Should we be enforcing this check server-side? This is where potential vulnerabilities could exist if not handled correctly. We need to be able to show business details, account details etc.

    Therefore, I must investigate the existing test suite. I'm going to consult `test/integration/helpdesk_api_test.rb` and `test/integration/edge_cases_test.rb`, to check if the tests for `email_verifications/confirm` or `password_resets/confirm` handle scenarios without the `X-Helpdesk-Account` header. In parallel, I'm going to `grep bad_request` across all `test/integration/*.rb` files to see if the missing header is covered as a test case.

messages.content:
I have implemented team invitations, user management & suspension, active staff listing, ticket assignment, and customer-isolated private notes in `/app`:

- **Team Invitations (`/api/v1/invitations`, `/api/v1/invitation_previews`, `/api/v1/invitation_acceptances`)**:
  - Added the `Invitation` model (`invitations` table) for `admin` and `agent` roles, hashing tokens with SHA-256 and emailing acceptance links to `/accept-invitation?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`.
  - Tracked `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked`, and `expired` statuses, ordered invitations by `id` ascending, and added `status` filtering, inspection (`GET /api/v1/invitations/:id`), token-rotating resend (`POST /api/v1/invitations/:id/resend`), and revocation (`DELETE /api/v1/invitations/:id`).
  - Prevented competing pending invitations, invitations to existing account emails, and customer registrations claiming emails with pending invitations.
  - Added `POST /api/v1/invitation_previews` and `POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances` so invited staff can preview invitation details and create an immediately verified user account without another verification email.
- **People Management & Staff Choices (`/api/v1/users`, `/api/v1/staff`)**:
  - Added `suspended` on users, exposed `GET /api/v1/users`, `GET /api/v1/users/:id`, and `PATCH/PUT /api/v1/users/:id` to admins only (ordered by `id` ascending, filterable by `role` and `suspended`).
  - Enforced that suspending a user revokes their active sessions, blocks sign-in, and clears their ticket assignments, while preventing suspension of the last active admin.
  - Added `GET /api/v1/staff` for active staff choices ordered by `id` ascending.
- **Ticket Assignments & Private Notes (`/api/v1/tickets`, `/api/v1/requests`)**:
  - Added `assignee_id` and `assignee` (`{ id, name }`) to tickets and supported assigning active staff or clearing with `null`.
  - Tracked `customer_updated_at` separately from internal ticket updates so internal activity (private notes with `public: false`, ticket assignments/unassignments, and suspension assignment clearing) never alters customer-facing `request` payloads or ordering.

Submitting the final output now.
